Repo /Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final (BMW requirements app "SharkSight"; Python 3.12 via `uv run`, SQLite data/app.db, FastAPI api/ on :8600 started with nohup — restart once at the end so exactly one server runs: `pgrep -fl "python -m api"`, kill it, `nohup uv run python -m api > <your scratchpad>/api.log 2>&1 &`; React 19 + Vite web/ on :5173 already running). SPEED MATTERS — the PM needs this soon for the demo. Ship a solid, working page fast; polish second. Read AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md (root; visual system, One Blue Rule, Definition/Prioritize sections), foundation/documents/challenge-brief.md (the DELIVERABLE list: per requirement ID, description, linked findings/sources, priority/score, prioritization rationale, evidence level, future-facing assumptions and uncertainties, decision status; BMW process step 5 "Documentation / tracking"), foundation/documents/requirement-definition.md and prioritization.md (incl. "As built").

Build **page 5 "Document"** (`/document`): the deliverable — the final, traceable requirement list per car line × market at the selected checkpoint.

Backend `api/routers/document.py` (register in api/routers/__init__.py before static; keep other lines):
- `GET /api/document?cp=&line=&market=` → for that line × market, all targets from the latest completed `prioritize` run at cp, ordered by confirmed band (PM decision) else AI band, then score. Each item: requirement key + a stable human ID (e.g. "REQ-5US-001" or reuse key), title, statement, domain, area (key/title/need), metric (name, unit, direction, conditions), acceptance criteria, the rung in use (PM's def_choice else AI recommended) with value + basis for this line × market, full ladder row, priority: AI score/band + PM-confirmed band/rationale/actor/date, prioritization rationale (prio_score.rationale), factor breakdown (compact), evidence level/confidence, evidence links (comments count + sample quotes with source ids, study items, research/web with URL + date + trust tier — reuse what /api/definition/requirement/{key} and /api/prioritize/target return; import their helpers rather than duplicating), assumptions + gaps + uncertainties, links to other requirements (relation, via), gates (brand/segment/market/feasibility), decision status (confirmed / AI proposal / open proposal against PM), history across checkpoints (cp1 → cp2 score/band, proposals and their outcome). Also a header: checkpoint label/cutoff, counts by band, number confirmed by PM, open proposals, generation timestamp, weights version.
- `GET /api/document/changes?line=&market=` → JAN → JUL diff: new requirements, removed, band up/down (AI and PM), PM decisions taken, proposals accepted/rejected.
- `GET /api/document/export?cp=&line=&market=&format=md|csv` → downloadable Markdown (readable deliverable with all fields + sources) and CSV (one row per requirement). Every export is logged as an audit_event (actor = PM/header actor, action `export`), like the old app did (check api/routers for an existing export pattern).
- Respect checkpoint visibility (cp1 must show nothing from cp2: proposals, decisions made at cp2 etc.). Note: a separate agent is fixing a proposal-visibility bug in api/routers/prioritize.py right now — don't edit that file; filter correctly in your own queries.
- Tests (tests/test_document.py): payload fields present, cp1 has no cp2 data, export logs an audit event. `uv run pytest -q` must not get worse than the 3 known legacy failures in tests/test_api.py.

Frontend (new files in web/src/screens/document/, types in web/src/lib/document.ts):
- Route `/document` + "Document" NavLink in PageSwitch (after Prioritize); add "document" to the mode unions the same way pages 3/4 did (App.tsx, Scan.tsx, Scene.tsx, Guide.tsx) — minimal additive edits; re-read each shared file right before editing; other sessions (e.g. 4e owns page transitions/animations; another agent is editing web/src/screens/prioritize/* and api/routers/prioritize.py) are active — never revert their hunks. Keep the transition SIMPLE: the 3D scene (car/skyline) sinks/dims behind a full-height document sheet (fade/slide ~300 ms, reduced-motion respected); don't touch the page-3/4 animation code beyond what's needed to dim it.
- Layout: a readable document view in the app's visual language (true black, Mona Sans, numerals lead, hairlines, no cards/shadows): top bar with car line + market switcher, checkpoint label, band counts, "n confirmed by PM", "n open proposals", Export (Markdown, CSV) buttons; a "Changes since JAN" toggle/section (at cp2); then the requirement list grouped by band (Must / Should / Could), each row compact (ID, title, domain mark, target value e.g. "≤ 18 min · projected", score, PM ✓ in blue only for PM-confirmed, evidence level, flags) and expandable to the full deliverable record (statement, metric + acceptance, ladder, rationale, factor breakdown, evidence with clickable sources, assumptions/gaps, links, gates, history). Search/filter by domain optional. Clicking "Open in Prioritize" goes to /prioritize with that target selected if trivial.
- Guide content for the page (Dock guide slot like pages 3/4) — short.

Verify: `cd web && npx tsc -b --noEmit` + `npm run build`; browser check with claude-in-chrome (one ToolSearch call: tabs_context_mcp, tabs_create_mcp, navigate, computer, read_console_messages) at /document?cp=cp1 and cp2 for 5 Series US and 5 Series CN, expand a record, test Markdown export (don't trigger dialogs), screenshot. Add a "Document (page 5)" section to DESIGN.md and a short "Document" section to foundation/documents/architecture.md or a new foundation/documents/document.md (additive). Don't commit; don't edit STATE.md/DECISIONS.md.

Final report (concise): files, endpoints, what's on screen, screenshot paths, tests/tsc/build, gaps.

# CLAUDE.md

@AGENTS.md

## Claude-specific notes

- `AGENTS.md` (imported above) is the canonical rule set shared with Codex and other agents — edit rules there, not here, so both stay in sync.
- The project memory is `foundation/` — read `foundation/README.md` for the read/write protocol. Prefer it over personal memory for anything project-related.
- The app's LLM provider is **OpenAI** (D-006) — don't add the Anthropic SDK or Claude model IDs to the app code.

# AGENTS.md

Hackathon project for the **BMW "AI for Product Decision Making"** challenge: an AI app that turns customer feedback, BMW product/sales data and web research into **prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements** for successor BMW vehicles, with a **product manager (PM) in the loop** and a **full audit trail**.

**Portfolio-level by design:** multiple models, markets, shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR → Neue Klasse) and plants from day one. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest example; F70 and G70 use the same pipeline. **LLM provider: OpenAI.** Stack: Python 3.12/uv, LangGraph, SQLite + sqlite-vec, no graph DB, Streamlit (D-015–D-020).

## Session start — mandatory

Read, in order (short):
1. `foundation/STATE.md` — phase, team, demo path, next steps, budget
2. `foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check for blockers
3. `foundation/DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table at the top; open full entries only when relevant. Don't re-open settled decisions without new info.

Then read only what your task needs:

| If your task touches… | Read |
|---|---|
| Scope, deliverables, what BMW asked | `documents/challenge-brief.md` |
| BMW data files, counts, quirks | `documents/data-inventory.md` |
| Stack / tooling, budget guard | `documents/tech-stack.md` |
| Workflow, entities, audit rules | `documents/architecture.md` |
| Requirement fields, evidence levels, scoring | `documents/requirement-model.md` |
| Research agents, trust tiers, brand/feasibility checks | `documents/knowledge-base.md` |
| Platforms, plants, BMW sales (cited) | `documents/portfolio-reference.md` (long — search it) |
| Competitors, trends, brand guardrails (cited) | `documents/competitor-landscape.md` (long — search it) |
| BMW Group Report 2025: deliveries, EV share, R&D, NK, digital | `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` |
| Unknown term or code | `documents/glossary.md` |
| Fresh clone / setup | `foundation/README.md` → Fresh clone |

## Session end — mandatory

- Update `foundation/STATE.md` (phase, in progress, next up, one-line session log entry with date).
- Log every decision as `D-xxx` in `foundation/DECISIONS.md`; new questions as `Q-xxx` in `foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`.
- If code changes the stack, schema, or workflow, update the matching doc in `foundation/documents/` in the same change.

## Core rules

1. **Raw data is read-only and confidential.** `challange information document/` (typo is the real folder name) is git-ignored — never modify, move or commit it; never send it anywhere except the agreed LLM provider. Derived data goes to git-ignored `data/`.
2. **Stay in scope.** Customer-facing requirements only (features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital, design & quality perception, driving experience, range/charging as experienced, variants/packages). **Out:** regulatory/homologation, engineering/component specs, pricing/business cases (rough effort as a factor is OK).
3. **Traceability is non-negotiable.** Every finding links to ≥1 source item; every requirement links to ≥1 finding. Keep provenance (file, sheet, row/ID, URL + date for web).
4. **Evidence vs. assumption.** Always separate evidence-backed statements from forward-looking assumptions (3–5 yr horizon); surface conflicting evidence instead of hiding it.
5. **The PM decides, never the AI.** AI only creates/edits in `proposed` status; `approved`/`rejected`/`deferred` require a human actor + rationale. Exception (D-013): AI may recompute *scores* of any requirement (logged); priority/status changes stay proposals.
6. **Audit everything, append-only.** Every change to requirement content, score, priority, evidence or status → an `audit_event` (actor human/ai/system, timestamp, before/after, rationale, model for AI).
7. **Portfolio, not one-offs.** Brands, models, markets, platforms and plants are data/config — never hardcode a derivative or market. Requirements can target several derivative × market combinations.
8. **Brand & segment fit.** Every requirement must fit the brand and the segment (no "cheap efficiency hatch" from BMW, no budget Rolls-Royce). Brand-fit `fail` blocks approval unless a PM overrides with rationale.
9. **Plant & platform feasibility.** A recommendation must be buildable: the derivative's platform and a plant that builds it can serve that market in time (incl. Neue Klasse transition). Used as a feasibility filter only — never output engineering specs. Whether a `fail` blocks approval is open (Q-010: BMW lists "architecture" as out of scope).
10. **Web evidence is cited evidence.** Competitor, sales, demand and expectation facts come from web research with URL, publish/retrieve date and trust tier (T1–T3). LLM opinions are never stored as sources; unverified user claims stay flagged until verified.
11. **Explainable prioritization.** Every score has a visible factor breakdown and plain-language rationale.
12. **OpenAI for all LLM work**; model names via env (`OPENAI_MODEL_*`). Secrets live in `.env` (git-ignored); commit `.env.example` only.
13. **Markets are different customers.** Climate, usage and culture differ — segment findings by market and score/prioritize each derivative × market separately; surface cross-market conflicts (D-011).
14. **Future, not just past.** Derive what customers will need at successor launch (3–5 yr) from predecessor feedback + competitors + trends; tag horizon, Kano class and assumptions (D-012).
15. **Living process, not a one-shot list.** ~2-year process: every prioritization run is snapshotted; AI only *proposes* priority/status changes with their cause; PM decides; history is always visible (D-013).
16. **$100 OpenAI budget, total.** Cheap model (`gpt-6-luna`) for bulk extraction/classification/summaries; `gpt-6.1-sol` only for reasoning-heavy steps; all calls through the budget-guarded wrapper; Flex/Batch + caching; capped web-search calls; pilot before full runs; update the Budget section in `foundation/STATE.md` after paid runs (D-010, thresholds D-014).
17. **Don't decide architecture alone.** The stack is fixed in D-015–D-020; changing it (new framework, store, LangChain, …) needs the team first. The demo data model is open (Q-017).
18. **Hackathon pace.** Ship a working demo path end-to-end before polishing; prefer simple, cached, deterministic pipelines over clever ones. Don't build what's not needed for the demo.

## Quick facts

- Datasets per vehicle: verbatims (xlsx), customer study (xlsx, CN/EU means + US 7-point distribution), sales volumes 2024/25/2030 (xlsx), German option price list (PDF).
- Feedback xlsx has **one row per classification** — dedupe by `ID` when counting verbatims.
- No China verbatims exist; US verbatims dominate G60/G70 (90–95%); F70 has no US data but ~⅓ Japan; almost no EU verbatims for G70. No dates in feedback.
- BMW sales volumes look stylized and conflict with public data (Q-015) — never blend them silently.
- Local anaconda Python is broken for pandas — use a `uv` venv (Python 3.12).

## Commits

Small, descriptive commits; don't commit unless asked. Never commit raw BMW data, `.env`, or local DBs.
- [No artifacts](no-artifacts.md) — never publish claude.ai Artifacts; keep pages as local files

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Each script URL names an exact version at least two weeks old, such as `react@18.3.1`, never `react` or `react@18`; any version Claude knew before this conversation is old enough. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Claude always authors the page as `.html`, and publishes a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly asks for one. When the person shares a Markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, Claude builds an HTML page from its content, keeping its substance and designing the page as it would any other artifact rather than transcribing the Markdown one to one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB work, but each artifact has its own origin and what a page stores lives only in that viewer's browser. It survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices or Claude. It can come back empty, or the accessor can throw, in a private window, with cleared or blocked site data, in previews or during thumbnail capture, so Claude wraps every read and write in try/catch and makes the page render correctly without it. Claude uses it only for per-viewer conveniences, such as a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section or an unsent draft, and never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers or be read back by Claude. That state belongs in a runtime capability.

**Size**: Claude keeps the rendered page at 16MB or smaller, and embedded `data:` URIs count toward that limit.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. Only the page itself is wrapped in a document skeleton at publish time: an HTML file in `files` is another page served without one, so Claude starts each with its own `<!doctype html>`, charset and viewport metas and base styles, or, without the doctype, it renders in quirks mode with browser defaults. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. Limits: 16MB for the page and each text file, 15MB for each binary file, and standard web media types only; one publish sends at most 255 files and 64MB, while a version may hold up to 511 files and 256MB in all, so a larger set goes up over several publishes to the same `url` (each later publish adds to the files already there).

**Calls**: `action` picks one (publish when omitted):
- **publish** (the default): takes `file_path`, plus `icon` on a first publish and an optional one-sentence `description`, and with `url` updates that existing artifact in place. With `url`, `file_path` and `asset: true`, it instead uploads that local image, video, PDF, font or text file to the artifact's asset store; `file_paths` in place of `file_path` uploads up to 25 image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in one call under one approval (a text file goes in a call of its own), and the result gives each one's `url`. The page must declare the `assets` capability, and the `artifact-capabilities` skill has the limits. Claude references the uploaded file from the page by the `url` in the result, exactly as given. To reuse assets another artifact already holds, such as a design system's fonts or images, Claude passes `from_url` (that artifact) and up to ten `asset_ids` from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it in place of `file_path`: the server copies them without downloading or re-uploading, and the result gives each copy's new url in this artifact, to reference exactly as given; both artifacts must be ones the person can open. Another artifact's published files are reused through `files` instead: Claude maps a path to {"artifact": "<its url>", "path": "<its published path>"} and that file is copied into the new version server side with its type. Script, style, data, font and image files copy this way, SVG images among them; an HTML or XML document does not, so Claude reads it with `path` and publishes it as its own file.
- **read**: takes `url` (any claude.ai artifact link: claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) and returns the published page's content. Claude reads these links with this action, not with WebFetch or curl, and also uses it wherever a skill or notice says to re-read an artifact. schema.name: Artifact
schema.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Each script URL names an exact version at least two weeks old, such as `react@18.3.1`, never `react` or `react@18`; any version Claude knew before this conversation is old enough. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Claude always authors the page as `.html`, and publishes a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly asks for one. When the person shares a Markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, Claude builds an HTML page from its content, keeping its substance and designing the page as it would any other artifact rather than transcribing the Markdown one to one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB work, but each artifact has its own origin and what a page stores lives only in that viewer's browser. action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

"""Prioritization (D-050, page 4): prio-v1 scores per requirement × car line × market at a checkpoint, bundles,
choose-jointly flags, proposals; PM confirms priorities and decides proposals — append-only (`prio_decision`) and
audited as human events (rule 5, 6). The AI never sets a confirmed priority.

GET  /api/prioritize?cp=                              targets, bundles, proposals, summary
GET  /api/prioritize/target/{key}?line=&market=&cp=   one target + history across checkpoints + evidence summary
GET  /api/prioritize/what-if?key=&line=&market=&level=&cp=   recompute for another rung, nothing stored
POST /api/prioritize/decision                         {key, line, market, priority, rationale, actor?, cp?, override_brand?}
POST /api/prioritize/proposal/{id}                    {verdict: accept|reject, rationale, actor?}
POST /api/prioritize/weights                          {factors, bands, rationale, actor?} → new prio-v1 weights version + re-score
GET  /api/prioritize/weights/history                  prio-v1 weights versions (revert = save an earlier one again)
POST /api/prioritize/preview                          {factors, bands, cp, line?, market?} → in-memory re-score, nothing stored

Decision, proposal verdict and weights queue an automatic re-score (`api/rescore.py`) after their commit and return
`rescore: queued`; GET /api/prioritize carries its `rescore` status.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel

from api import rescore as R
from api.deps import conflict, db, get_actor, need_rationale, not_found
from bmw_req.checkpoints import BY_ID, CHECKPOINTS, CheckpointError, latest_run, visible_ids
from bmw_req.pipeline.requirements import audit
from bmw_req.prioritize import ensure
from bmw_req.prioritize import score as P

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/prioritize", tags=["prioritize"])
DIM_ORDER = ("customer", "business", "future")


def _loads(s, default=None):
    return json.loads(s) if s else default


def _runs(conn, cp: str) -> dict:
    if cp not in BY_ID:
        raise not_found(f"No checkpoint {cp!r}")
    ensure(conn)
    return {s: latest_run(conn, cp, s) for s in ("prioritize", "gate")}


def _run_view(r) -> dict | None:
    return {"id": r["id"], "finished_at": r["finished_at"], "stats": _loads(r["stats_json"], {})} if r else None


def _reqs(conn, run_id: int | None) -> dict[str, dict]:
    if not run_id:
        return {}
    return {r["key"]: dict(r) for r in conn.execute("SELECT key, title, domain, zones_json, area_key FROM def_requirement WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,))}


def _target(row, req: dict | None, decided: dict | None, state: str | None, prev: dict | None) -> dict:
    b = _loads(row["breakdown_json"], {})
    conf = _loads(row["confidence_json"], {})
    factors = sorted(({"key": k, "dimension": f.get("dimension"), "label": f.get("label"), "value": f.get("value"), "weight": f.get("weight"),
                       "points": f.get("points") or 0, "explanation": f.get("explanation"), "available": f.get("available"),
                       **({"method": f["method"]} if "method" in f else {})} for k, f in b.get("factors", {}).items()),
                     key=lambda f: DIM_ORDER.index(f["dimension"]) if f["dimension"] in DIM_ORDER else 9)
    return {"key": row["req_key"], "version": row["req_version"], "title": (req or {}).get("title"), "domain": (req or {}).get("domain"),
            "zones": _loads((req or {}).get("zones_json"), []), "area_key": (req or {}).get("area_key"),
            "line": row["line"], "market": row["market"], "score": row["score"], "base": row["base"], "band": row["band"],
            "own_band": b.get("own_priority"),
            "confirmed": {"priority": decided["priority"], "actor": decided["actor"], "at": decided["created_at"],
                          "rationale": decided["rationale"]} if decided else None,
            "rank": row["rank"], "state": state,
            "confidence": {"level": conf.get("level"), "mult": conf.get("mult"), "basis_mix": conf.get("basis_mix"),
                           "basis_score": conf.get("basis_score"), "comments": conf.get("comments"), "study": conf.get("study")},
            "factors": factors, "modifiers": _loads(row["modifiers_json"], []), "gates": b.get("gate_detail") or {},
            "bundle_id": row["bundle_id"], "flags": _loads(row["flags_json"], []),
            "rung": {"chosen": (b.get("rung") or {}).get("chosen"), "recommended": (b.get("rung") or {}).get("recommended"),
                     "by": (b.get("rung") or {}).get("by")},
            "effort": b.get("effort"), "gaps": b.get("gaps", []), "rationale": row["rationale"],
            "prev": {"score": prev["score"], "band": prev["band"], "checkpoint": prev.get("checkpoint")} if prev else None}


def _prev_band(conn, run) -> dict[tuple, dict]:
    if not run or not run["parent_run_id"]:
        return {}
    cp = conn.execute("SELECT checkpoint_id FROM checkpoint_run WHERE id = ?", (run["parent_run_id"],)).fetchone()[0]
    return {(r["req_key"], r["line"], r["market"]): {"score": r["score"], "band": r["band"], "checkpoint": cp}
            for r in conn.execute("SELECT req_key, line, market, score, band FROM prio_score WHERE run_id = ?", (run["parent_run_id"],))}


def _states(conn, run_id: int) -> dict[tuple, str]:
    out = {}
    for r in conn.execute("SELECT entity_key, state FROM track WHERE run_id = ? AND entity_key LIKE 'prio:%'", (run_id,)):
        k, line, m = r["entity_key"][5:].split("|")
        out[(k, line, m)] = r["state"]
    return out


def _proposal(r) -> dict:
    fd = _loads(r["factor_delta_json"], {})
    return {"id": r["id"], "run_id": r["run_id"], "key": r["req_key"], "line": r["line"], "market": r["market"], "old_band": r["old_band"],
            "proposed_band": r["proposed_band"], "cause": r["cause"], "factor_delta": fd.get("points", {}),
            "explain": fd.get("explain"), "against": fd.get("against"), "score": fd.get("score"), "prev_score": fd.get("prev_score"),
            "status": r["status"], "decided_by": r["decided_by"], "decided_at": r["decided_at"],
            "decision_rationale": r["decision_rationale"], "created_at": r["created_at"]}


def _visible_proposals(conn, cp: str, run_id: int) -> list[dict]:
    """Proposals a PM at `cp` may see: those of the current run, plus still-open ones from earlier runs at checkpoints
    visible at `cp` (cp1 sees cp1 only; cp2 sees cp1 + cp2) — never a later checkpoint's. One open proposal per target:
    the newest wins."""
    vis = visible_ids(cp)
    rows = conn.execute(f"""SELECT p.* FROM prio_proposal p JOIN checkpoint_run r ON r.id = p.run_id
                            WHERE r.checkpoint_id IN ({','.join('?' * len(vis))}) AND (p.run_id = ? OR p.status = 'open')
                            ORDER BY p.id""", (*vis, run_id)).fetchall()
    newest_open = {}
    for r in rows:
        if r["status"] == "open":
            newest_open[(r["req_key"], r["line"], r["market"])] = r["id"]
    return [_proposal(r) for r in rows if r["status"] != "open" or newest_open[(r["req_key"], r["line"], r["market"])] == r["id"]]


@router.get("")
def prioritize(cp: str = Query("cp2")) -> dict:
    with db() as conn:
        runs = _runs(conn, cp)
        wid, weights, bands = P.stored_config(conn)
        base = {"checkpoint": cp, "runs": {s: _run_view(r) for s, r in runs.items()},
                "weights": {"scheme": P.SCHEME, "version": wid, "factors": weights, "bands": bands,
                            "defaults": {"factors": P.DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, "bands": P.DEFAULT_BANDS}},
                "rescore": R.status(),
                "dimensions": P.DIMENSION,
                "labels": {"market_weight": "stylized (Q-015)", "market_weight_note": P.MARKET_LABEL}}
        run = runs["prioritize"]
        if not run:
            return {**base, "ready": False, "lines": [], "markets": [], "targets": [], "bundles": [], "proposals": [], "summary": {}}
        stats = _loads(run["stats_json"], {})
        reqs = _reqs(conn, (stats.get("upstream") or {}).get("define"))
        decided, prev, states = P.decisions_at(conn, cp), _prev_band(conn, run), _states(conn, run["id"])
        targets = [_target(r, reqs.get(r["req_key"]), decided.get((r["req_key"], r["line"], r["market"])),
                           states.get((r["req_key"], r["line"], r["market"])), prev.get((r["req_key"], r["line"], r["market"])))
                   for r in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM prio_score WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY line, market, rank", (run["id"],))]
        bundles = [{"id": r["bundle_id"], "keys": _loads(r["keys_json"], []), **(_loads(r["relations_json"], {}) or {}),
                    "band_by_target": _loads(r["band_by_target_json"], {})}
                   for r in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM prio_bundle WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY id", (run["id"],))]
        keys = {t["key"] for t in targets}
        proposals = [p for p in _visible_proposals(conn, cp, run["id"]) if p["key"] in keys]
        lines = sorted({t["line"] for t in targets})
        markets = sorted({t["market"] for t in targets})
        return {**base, "ready": True, "lines": lines, "markets": markets, "targets": targets, "bundles": bundles,
                "proposals": proposals, "summary": {"by_band": stats.get("by_band"), "by_market": stats.get("by_market"),
                                                    "flags": stats.get("flags"), "competitive_method": stats.get("competitive_method")}}


@router.get("/target/{key:path}")
def target(key: str, line: str = Query(...), market: str = Query(...), cp: str = Query("cp2")) -> dict:
    with db() as conn:
        runs = _runs(conn, cp)
        run = runs["prioritize"]
        if not run:
            raise not_found("No prioritize run at this checkpoint")
        row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM prio_score WHERE run_id = ? AND req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ?",
                           (run["id"], key, line, market)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise not_found(f"No target {key} × {line} × {market} at {cp}")
        stats = _loads(run["stats_json"], {})
        reqs = _reqs(conn, (stats.get("upstream") or {}).get("define"))
        decided = P.decisions_at(conn, cp)
        out = _target(row, reqs.get(key), decided.get((key, line, market)), _states(conn, run["id"]).get((key, line, market)),
                      _prev_band(conn, run).get((key, line, market)))
        history = []
        for c in CHECKPOINTS:
            if c.position > BY_ID[cp].position:
                continue
            r = latest_run(conn, c.id, "prioritize")
            h = conn.execute("SELECT score, band, rank, rung, rationale FROM prio_score WHERE run_id = ? AND req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ?",
                             (r["id"], key, line, market)).fetchone() if r else None
            if h:
                dc = P.decisions_at(conn, c.id).get((key, line, market))
                history.append({"checkpoint": c.id, "label": c.label, "run_id": r["id"], **dict(h),
                                "confirmed": dc["priority"] if dc else None})
        req = conn.execute("SELECT evidence_ids_json, trend_ids_json, statement FROM def_requirement WHERE run_id = ? AND key = ?",
                           ((stats.get("upstream") or {}).get("define"), key)).fetchone()
        ev = _loads(req["evidence_ids_json"], []) if req else []
        kinds = defaultdict(int)
        for i in ev:
            kinds[i.split(":")[0]] += 1
        vis = visible_ids(cp)
        decisions = [dict(x) for x in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT * FROM prio_decision WHERE req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ? AND (checkpoint_id IS NULL OR checkpoint_id IN "
            f"({','.join('?' * len(vis))})) ORDER BY id", (key, line, market, *vis))]
        proposals = [_proposal(x) for x in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT p.* FROM prio_proposal p JOIN checkpoint_run r ON r.id = p.run_id WHERE p.req_key = ? AND p.line = ? AND p.market = ? "
            f"AND r.checkpoint_id IN ({','.join('?' * len(vis))}) ORDER BY p.id", (key, line, market, *vis))]
        return {**out, "statement": req["statement"] if req else None, "history": history, "decisions": decisions, "proposals": proposals,
                "evidence": {"comments": out["confidence"]["comments"], "study": kinds.get("study", 0), "research": kinds.get("research", 0),
                             "options": kinds.get("option", 0), "insights": kinds.get("insight", 0),
                             "own_market": "borrowed_voice" not in out["flags"], "count": len(ev), "by_kind": dict(kinds), "trend_ids": _loads(req["trend_ids_json"], []) if req else [],
                             "factors": {f["key"]: f["explanation"] for f in out["factors"]}}}


@router.get("/what-if")
def what_if(key: str = Query(...), line: str = Query(...), market: str = Query(...),
            level: Literal["baseline", "threshold", "target", "stretch"] = Query(...), cp: str = Query("cp2")) -> dict:
    with db() as conn:
        _runs(conn, cp)
        try:
            return P.what_if(conn, cp, key, line, market, level)
        except CheckpointError as e:
            raise conflict(str(e)) from e
        except KeyError as e:
            raise not_found(str(e)) from e


class DecisionBody(BaseModel):
    key: str
    line: str
    market: str
    priority: Literal["Must", "Should", "Could"]
    rationale: str
    actor: str | None = None
    cp: str | None = None
    override_brand: bool = False


class ProposalBody(BaseModel):
    verdict: Literal["accept", "reject"]
    rationale: str
    actor: str | None = None


class WeightsBody(BaseModel):
    factors: dict[str, float] | None = None
    weights: dict[str, float] | None = None     # legacy name of `factors`
    bands: dict[str, float] | None = None       # {Must, Should}; omitted = keep the current thresholds
    rationale: str
    actor: str | None = None


class PreviewBody(BaseModel):
    factors: dict[str, float]
    bands: dict[str, float]
    cp: str = "cp2"
    line: str | None = None
    market: str | None = None


def _gate_brand(conn, key: str, line: str, market: str, cp: str | None) -> str | None:
    for c in ([cp] if cp in BY_ID else []) + [c.id for c in reversed(CHECKPOINTS)]:
        r = latest_run(conn, c, "gate")
        if r:
            g = conn.execute("SELECT result FROM prio_fit WHERE run_id = ? AND req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ? AND check_type = 'brand' "
                             "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1", (r["id"], key, line, market)).fetchone()
            return g["result"] if g else None
    return None


def _decide(conn, key: str, line: str, market: str, priority: str, why: str, actor: str, cp: str | None, extra: dict) -> tuple[int, dict | None]:
    """Insert a prio_decision + human audit_event (caller holds the transaction)."""
    before = conn.execute("SELECT priority, rationale, actor, checkpoint_id FROM prio_decision WHERE req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ? "
                          "ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1", (key, line, market)).fetchone()
    cur = conn.execute("INSERT INTO prio_decision (req_key, line, market, priority, rationale, actor, checkpoint_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                       (key, line, market, priority, why, actor, cp))
    audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action="confirm_priority", entity_type="prio_target", entity_id=f"{key}|{line}|{market}",
          field="priority", old=dict(before) if before else None, new={"priority": priority, "checkpoint": cp, **extra}, rationale=why)
    return cur.lastrowid, dict(before) if before else None


@router.post("/decision")
def decision(body: DecisionBody, header_actor: str = Depends(get_actor)) -> dict:
    why = need_rationale(body.rationale)
    actor = (body.actor or "").strip() or header_actor
    with db() as conn:
        ensure(conn)
        cp = body.cp if body.cp in BY_ID else None
        ai = conn.execute("SELECT band, score FROM prio_score WHERE req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ? ORDER BY run_id DESC LIMIT 1",
                          (body.key, body.line, body.market)).fetchone()
        if ai is None:
            raise not_found(f"No scored target {body.key} × {body.line} × {body.market}")
        brand = _gate_brand(conn, body.key, body.line, body.market, cp)
        if brand == "fail" and body.priority in ("Must", "Should") and not body.override_brand:
            raise conflict("Brand-fit FAIL: confirming this priority needs override_brand with a rationale (D-008).")
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            did, before = _decide(conn, body.key, body.line, body.market, body.priority, why, actor, cp,
                                  {"ai_band": ai["band"], "ai_score": ai["score"], "brand_gate": brand, "override_brand": body.override_brand})
            seen_at = [c.id for c in CHECKPOINTS if cp is None or cp in visible_ids(c.id)]   # the decision applies here
            conn.execute(f"UPDATE prio_proposal SET status = 'superseded' WHERE req_key = ? AND line = ? AND market = ? AND status = 'open' "
                         f"AND run_id IN (SELECT id FROM checkpoint_run WHERE checkpoint_id IN ({','.join('?' * len(seen_at))}))",
                         (body.key, body.line, body.market, *seen_at))
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except BaseException:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
    # inputs at the decision's checkpoint are unchanged: re-score the LATER checkpoints against the PM's band
    rs = R.queue(cp or CHECKPOINTS[0].id, "decision", include_self=False)
    return {"ok": True, "id": did, "decision": {"key": body.key, "line": body.line, "market": body.market, "priority": body.priority,
                                                "rationale": why, "actor": actor}, "before": before, "rescore": rs}


@router.post("/proposal/{pid}")
def proposal(pid: int, body: ProposalBody, header_actor: str = Depends(get_actor)) -> dict:
    why = need_rationale(body.rationale)
    actor = (body.actor or "").strip() or header_actor
    with db() as conn:
        ensure(conn)
        p = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM prio_proposal WHERE id = ?", (pid,)).fetchone()
        if p is None:
            raise not_found(f"No proposal {pid}")
        if p["status"] != "open":
            raise conflict(f"Proposal {pid} is {p['status']}, not open")
        cp = conn.execute("SELECT checkpoint_id FROM checkpoint_run WHERE id = ?", (p["run_id"],)).fetchone()[0]
        if body.verdict == "accept" and p["proposed_band"] in ("Must", "Should") and \
                _gate_brand(conn, p["req_key"], p["line"], p["market"], cp) == "fail":
            raise conflict("Brand-fit FAIL: accept via POST /decision with override_brand and a rationale (D-008).")
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            status = "accepted" if body.verdict == "accept" else "rejected"
            conn.execute("UPDATE prio_proposal SET status = ?, decided_by = ?, decided_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'), "
                         "decision_rationale = ? WHERE id = ?", (status, actor, why, pid))
            audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action=f"proposal_{status}", entity_type="prio_proposal", entity_id=str(pid),
                  field="status", old={"status": "open", "band": p["old_band"]},
                  new={"status": status, "proposed_band": p["proposed_band"], "cause": p["cause"]}, rationale=why)
            did = None
            if status == "accepted":
                did, _ = _decide(conn, p["req_key"], p["line"], p["market"], p["proposed_band"], why, actor, cp,
                                 {"via_proposal": pid, "cause": p["cause"]})
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except BaseException:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
    rs = R.queue(cp, f"proposal_{status}", include_self=False)

@router.post("/weights")
def weights(body: WeightsBody, header_actor: str = Depends(get_actor)) -> dict:
    """New prio-v1 weights version (factors + band thresholds) + human audit_event, then an automatic re-score of every
    checkpoint (cp1 → cp2); PM-confirmed bands that now differ get a `weights_changed` proposal, never a silent change."""
    why = need_rationale(body.rationale)
    actor = (body.actor or "").strip() or header_actor
    factors = body.factors if body.factors is not None else body.weights
    if factors is None:
        raise conflict("factors are required")
    with db() as conn:
        ensure(conn)
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            wid = P.set_weights(conn, factors, actor, why, body.bands)
            conn.execute("COMMIT")
        except ValueError as e:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise conflict(str(e)) from e
        except BaseException:
            conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        _, f, b = P.stored_config(conn)
    rs = R.queue(None, "weights_changed")
    return {"ok": True, "weights_version": wid, "factors": f, "weights": f, "bands": b, "rescore": rs}

283	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")

494	def bundles(links: list[dict], keys: set[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
495	    """Connected components over links with strength ≥ 2 that the PM has not removed (union-find)."""
496	    parent: dict[str, str] = {}
497	
498	    def find(x):
499	        parent.setdefault(x, x)
500	        while parent[x] != x:
501	            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
502	            x = parent[x]
503	        return x
504	
505	    use = [l for l in links if (l.get("strength") or 0) >= 2 and (l.get("review") or {}).get("verdict") != "removed"
506	           and (keys is None or (l["a"] in keys and l["b"] in keys))]
507	    for l in use:
508	        parent[find(l["a"])] = find(l["b"])
509	    comp = defaultdict(set)
510	    for l in use:
511	        comp[find(l["a"])].update((l["a"], l["b"]))
512	    out = []
513	    for i, ks in enumerate(sorted(comp.values(), key=lambda s: (-len(s), sorted(s)[0]))):
514	        inner = [l for l in use if l["a"] in ks]
515	        rel = defaultdict(int)
516	        for l in inner:
517	            rel[f"{l['relation']} via {l['via']}"] += 1
518	        out.append({"id": f"bundle:{i + 1}", "keys": sorted(ks), "conflict": any(l["relation"] == "conflicts" for l in inner),
519	                    "reason": ", ".join(f"{k} ×{n}" if n > 1 else k for k, n in sorted(rel.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))})
520	    return out

527	    for l in (conn.execute("SELECT * FROM def_link WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY id", (run_id,)) if run_id else []):
528	        k = (l["a_key"], l["b_key"], l["relation"])
529	        seen.add(k)
530	        out.append({"id": "|".join(k), "a": l["a_key"], "b": l["b_key"], "relation": l["relation"], "via": l["via"],
531	                    "strength": l["strength"], "direction": l["direction"], "rationale": l["rationale"], "method": l["method"],
532	                    "state": (states.get("|".join(k)) or {}).get("state"), "review": reviews.get(k), "source": "ai"})
533	    for k, rv in reviews.items():   # links the PM added
534	        if k not in seen and rv["verdict"] == "added" and k[0] in keys and k[1] in keys:
535	            out.append({"id": "|".join(k), "a": k[0], "b": k[1], "relation": k[2], "via": rv["via"], "strength": rv["strength"] or 2,
536	                        "direction": "mutual", "rationale": rv["rationale"], "method": "pm", "state": "added", "review": rv,
537	                        "source": "pm"})
538	    return out
